synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The PR is sold as a type-only refactor but ships two real behavior changes: an empty-domain throw replacing silent [NaN, NaN], and a coerceNumber wrapper that maps null to 0 where the old toNumber pipeline would have produced NaN. The peek overload and Domain/Anchor type work are sound, but the non-emptiness invariant is now duplicated (overload + runtime guard) and Domain is typed wider than its true two-endpoint contract. The panel recommends splitting the patch, preserving prior null/NaN semantics or documenting the change, picking one source of truth for non-emptiness, and extending the empty-domain tests to Log/Pow/Symlog.

issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null/undefined to 0 where the old toNumber pipeline produced NaN, a semantic shift hidden in a refactor.
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear used toNumber directly, so non-numeric domain entries propagated as NaN. The new local coerceNumber returns 0 on null via `?? 0`, silently turning bad input into a finite-but-wrong domain. This is a runtime behavior change smuggled into a type-only PR. Preserve toNumber's return shape or document and test the new semantics.

issues.description: PR labeled as type-only but introduces a new runtime throw on empty domains, a real behavior change.
issues.detail: The commit claims 'same runtime behavior as before,' yet the diff adds `error('Domain array must not be empty')` on a path that previously returned [NaN, NaN] silently. Callers depending on the old silent path will now throw. Split this out as its own commit with a changelog note, or rename the PR to reflect the behavior change.

issues.description: Non-emptiness invariant is enforced twice — via the peek overload in the type system and via isNonEmpty at runtime.
issues.detail: The new peek overload already proves non-emptiness statically, but the body re-proves it with isNonEmpty and a throw. Pick one source of truth: either narrow the parameter to NonEmptyArray<number> and push the check to the edge, or keep the runtime guard and drop the overload ceremony. Today the same fact lives in two places.

issues.description: Domain is typed `number[]` but the algorithm only consumes two endpoints, hiding the real contract.
issues.detail: pan/zoom use only domain[0] and peek(domain), so a caller passing [1,2,3,4] silently has the middle ignored. Either accept NonEmptyArray<number> or a readonly tuple like [number, number] so the type tells the same story as the algorithm. Also, length-1 arrays pass isNonEmpty but violate the two-distinct-endpoints invariant.

issues.description: Empty-domain test coverage is partial — only Linear variants are tested; Log/Pow/Symlog are unverified.
issues.detail: panLinear and zoomLinear get t.throws cases, but panLog/panPow/panSymlog and their zoom counterparts share the guard transitively through pan/zoom and remain untested. If anyone later inlines or refactors those helpers, the regression will not be caught. A few parameterized cases would lock the contract for all six exported functions.

issues.description: Local identity reimplementation forks a concept that already exists in accessors.js.
issues.detail: The old code imported identity from './accessors.js'; the new file inlines `const identity: TransformFn = x => x` instead. If accessors.identity has the wrong type, fix it at the source rather than creating a parallel name in this module. Bad taste, and it complicates future refactors that touch the shared helper.
